analysis: Integration of the prior analyses and replayed patches. Reported three medium findings: (1) the dev-branch lane signs unreviewed code with the production Developer ID and passes `secrets: inherit` (docs/operations/provider-release.md:527); (2) release-derived public cluster qualifications are admitted on any Apple silicon pair without tested placements and are not covered by the threat model (provider-release.md:659); (3) the parity qualification in ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:331 is a compile-time constant that is not bound to the evidence run's build. Replayed source covers the composite action shard logic (inputs passed via env, regex-validated K/N, qualification lane only), the ci.yml test addition, the release-dev-branch/release-swift path filters and the part-health.json split in ClusterServiceAgent.swift. I found no injection or regression in them. Unverified contracts need follow-up: the `qualify-sdk` aggregator in release-provider.yml has no `!cancelled()`, so a shard failure makes it skipped. Whether the build-and-release `if` (base text indicated it requires 'success', or both skipped on resume) and scripts/provider_release_resume/identity.py treat skipped as non-passing needs confirmation. The audit in scripts/provider-test-shards.py, which must detect missing shards, is not visible. The cluster-runtime facts step runs the built app after the signing keychain is deleted, and job-level env and secrets residue is unseen. The coordinator's validation of cluster_runtime is platform-owned. The health-file PID check and file permissions code was not supplied. Only a subset of source units was replayed (222 omitted), so deeper review remains warranted.

findings.detail: The new dev-branch lane builds, signs (the same Developer ID signature as master), notarizes and registers every push to `dev`. The registered build is a trusted official-build identity on the dev coordinator. The doc says review is not enforced on `dev` today and defers the fix to a pull_request rule that an administrator adds later. The lane also calls the reusable workflow with `secrets: inherit`, which exposes every repository secret including PROD_* and STAGING_*. Only a test pins the guards that keep those secrets from being read. A single bypass-list account, or a compromised one, could ship unreviewed code that is notarized and registered as a trusted build. A change to the reusable workflow could also read production secrets. The threat model does not cover this release-signing path. Fix: land the pull_request/CODEOWNERS rule before enabling the lane, pass only named secrets instead of `secrets: inherit`, and record the dev signing path in the threat model.
findings.title: Documented dev-branch lane signs unreviewed code with the production Developer ID, with the review rule not yet enforced

findings.detail: The new `cluster_runtime` block makes a coordinator derive pair approvals, pair-serving grants and public parity qualifications from every signed release. The docs say these qualifications apply to the whole mode family on any Apple silicon pair, and admit that no pipeline run of either model happened on two M5 Ultras and that GLM has no tensor-parallel cross-cable record. The admission rests on an owner decision, not tested placements. Public consumer prompts (A-001) are then split across two provider Macs, with intermediate activations crossing a LAN link. Neither the retained TB-002/TB-007 text nor T-007 and T-056 addresses confidentiality of that inter-member link, trust in the second provider, or correctness of unqualified placements. Both providers are adversarial in this model. Fix: bind qualifications to tested numerics classes and placements, and add a threat-model entry for cluster routing covering member trust and the inter-member channel before public routing is enabled.
findings.title: Release-derived public cluster qualifications admit consumer traffic on unqualified placements; threat model lacks cluster routing coverage

findings.detail: parityQualifications() (ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift:331-333) hardcodes promotable:true, diverged:false, a constant evidenceSHA256 and a constant qualifiedAt (ClusterPublicModels.swift:46-48). It derives the numerics class from whatever metallib the release ships, combined with hardcoded hardware ranks. Any build whose worker reports the two declared artifact hashes is emitted as parity-qualified for public traffic with a 1M-token envelope, even if the metallib, worker or placement code changed since the 2026-10-31 evidence run. Nothing in the facts ties the qualification to the evidence run's build or digests; the only link is a test that the constant equals the hash of a doc. A coordinator that derives approvals from these facts (outside the supplied evidence) will treat the claim as qualification, so a regressed or divergent numerics build could be admitted to serve public consumers. Fix: bind the qualification to the qualified metallib/worker/placement digests, or require the coordinator to check them against allowlisted evidence-run digests, and re-run parity evidence on metallib changes.
findings.title: Public-traffic parity qualifications are asserted from compile-time constants for any build, not bound to evidence for that build
